text:
maria: heads-up — main is red on the integration matrix. failing test is tests/integration/test_sessions.py::test_session_cleanup. circleci job circleci/gh-int/5123.
raj: saw that, reran the job once (5123.1) and it failed again with the same teardown AssertionError.
ci-bot: build failed: https://circleci.com/gh/redwood-inference/5123 — junit attached at artifacts/5123/junit.xml
kai: any recent dependency bumps? I glanced at the lockfile PR that merged earlier (deps: httpx 0.24.0 -> 0.25.0, urllib3 pin changes)
maria: yes that lock-bump PR landed this morning — felt small but tests hit sessions and flaky teardown started after merge.
olivia: error looks like "AssertionError: expected session to have been closed" during async shutdown. Could be behavior change in httpx or our internal client wrapper.
raj: can someone try reproducing locally quickly? steps I used: `git checkout main && poetry install --no-dev && pytest tests/integration/test_sessions.py::test_session_cleanup -q`
maria: repro on linux in docker worked for me. failing consistently.
kai: request: can we bisect to find which transitive upgrade caused it? try `poetry lock --no-update` vs using the previous lockfile from yesterday.
jamie: I can take the bisect. plan: checkout yesterday's lockfile from PR before merge, run CI locally via `scripts/ci/run_integration.sh --job sessions` and then do binary search on merged commits.
olivia: +1 — also check wheels/artifacts: there was a difference in `urllib3` wheel tags on the mac runners earlier this week. maybe relevant if we have session pooling semantics changed.
raj: short-term mitigation: revert the lock bump on main or pin the httpx/httpcore combination to previous known-good. we should decide quickly because nightly run will hit more infra.
maria: can jamie run bisect and post the first-green/first-red commit? also please include `pip freeze` and `poetry show --tree` from repro env.
ci-bot: requested action: assign @jamie to issue redwood/ci#784
jamie: starting bisect now, will post updates here. ETA ~45m.
raj: if bisect points to httpx/httpcore, we can try switching to 0.24.x combo and run full integration suite on a branch while we investigate.
maria: thanks everyone. tagging @kai as infra owner for followup on any runner-specific wheel fallout.
jamie: first bisect result: commit abcdef2 introduced transitive `rfc3986` bump, commit abcdef5 switched httpx -> 0.25.0. first-red is abcdef5, first-green abcdef4. digging into delta now.
olivia: nice — if httpx 0.25.0 is suspect, try installing httpx==0.24.0 with current lock and rerun one CI job to confirm.
raj: I'll open a revert/patch PR if jamie confirms. if it's flaky-only on some runners, we may instead add a short-term test skip with linked tracking issue.
jamie: confirmed: pinning httpx==0.24.0 in the environment fixed the test locally. raising PR to pin and adding regression note.
maria: great. please include changelog line and link to CI job in the PR description. deploybot, once PR merges, let's trigger a full integration matrix run.
ci-bot: action queued: rerun integration matrix after PR merge.
raj: cheers — good quick triage. will follow up on making the bisect steps a tiny script for next time.
